questions.text: At which type of plate boundary do two plates move apart?

feedback: At destructive boundaries plates move towards each other and one sinks
At conservative boundaries plates slide past each other
At collision zones two continental plates push together

questions.solution: At a constructive boundary plates move apart and magma rises to form new crust
questions.hint: New crust is made where magma rises between the plates

questions.text: What is the point on the Earth's surface directly above where an earthquake starts called? Give the term.

feedback.focus: The focus is the point underground where the earthquake starts
feedback.hypocentre: The hypocentre (focus) is the point underground where the earthquake starts
feedback.hypocenter: The hypocentre (focus) is the point underground where the earthquake starts

questions.solution: The epicentre is on the surface directly above the focus, where the earthquake starts underground
questions.hint: It is directly above the focus

questions.text: What is a tropical storm called when it forms in the north-west Pacific, near the Philippines and Japan?

feedback: Hurricanes form in the Atlantic and north-east Pacific
Cyclones form in the Indian Ocean and South Pacific
A tornado is a much smaller spinning column of air over land

questions.solution: Tropical storms are called typhoons in the north-west Pacific
questions.hint: Hurricanes form in the Atlantic; this is a different name used in East Asia

questions.text: What is the name for a series of large sea waves caused by an undersea earthquake? Give the term.
questions.solution: An undersea earthquake can lift the seabed and push up the water, causing a tsunami
questions.hint: The word comes from Japanese and means harbour wave

questions.text: Which type of volcano has gentle slopes and runny lava?

feedback: Composite volcanoes are steep, with layers of ash and sticky lava
Lava domes are steep mounds of very sticky lava

questions.solution: Shield volcanoes are built from runny basalt lava that flows a long way, giving gentle slopes
questions.hint: Its shape is like a warrior's shield lying on the ground

questions.text: What instrument records the shaking of the ground during an earthquake? Give its name.
questions.solution: A seismometer (seismograph) records ground movement
questions.hint: Its name begins with the Greek word for shaking

questions.text: Which of these is a SECONDARY effect of an earthquake?

options: Buildings collapsing as the ground shakes
Fires caused by broken gas pipes

questions.solution: Secondary effects follow later as a result of the primary effects, such as fires from broken gas pipes
questions.hint: Primary effects happen during the shaking itself

questions.text: What type of plate boundary is the San Andreas Fault in California?
questions.solution: At the San Andreas Fault the Pacific and North American plates slide past each other
questions.hint: The plates move sideways past each other here

questions.text: What is the calm area at the centre of a tropical storm called?

feedback: The eyewall is the ring of the strongest winds and heaviest rain around the centre
A storm surge is a rise in sea level pushed onto land

questions.solution: The eye is calm, with sinking air and low pressure
questions.hint: It is in the very middle of the storm

questions.text: What is the term for a fast-moving cloud of very hot gas, ash and rock that flows down the side of a volcano? Give the term.
questions.solution: Pyroclastic flows can move at over 100 km/h and are very dangerous
questions.hint: Its name comes from the Greek words for fire and broken

questions.text: Which scale measures the strength of hurricanes from category 1 to 5? Give its name.
questions.solution: The Saffir-Simpson scale rates hurricanes from category 1 to 5 by wind speed
questions.hint: It is named after an engineer and a meteorologist

questions.text: Which of these is a human cause of climate change?

feedback: Changes in the Earth's orbit are a natural cause
Volcanic eruptions are a natural cause
Changes in the Sun's output are a natural cause

questions.solution: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide, which increases the greenhouse effect
questions.hint: Look for the one that people do

questions.text: A city builds houses with rubber shock absorbers in their foundations and cross-bracing in the walls. Which hazard is it preparing for?
questions.solution: Shock absorbers and cross-bracing help buildings survive ground shaking
questions.hint: Think about which hazard shakes buildings from below

questions.text: Why does Iceland have so many volcanoes?

options: Iceland lies on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, a constructive plate boundary
Iceland lies on a conservative plate boundary
Iceland is part of the Pacific Ring of Fire
Iceland is at a collision zone like the Himalayas
feedback: Conservative boundaries have earthquakes but no volcanoes
Iceland is in the North Atlantic, not the Pacific

questions.solution: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where plates move apart and magma rises
questions.hint: Find Iceland on a map of plate boundaries

questions.text: Tropical storms need warm sea water to form. Which temperature is closest to the minimum sea surface temperature they need?
questions.solution: Tropical storms usually need sea surface temperatures of about 26–27°C or more
questions.hint: The sea must be warmer than a typical British summer day

questions.text: Scientists study air bubbles trapped in ice from deep inside the Antarctic ice sheet. What evidence are they using?

options: Tree rings, to show past climate
Ice cores, to show past climate

questions.solution: Ice cores contain trapped air that shows past carbon dioxide levels and temperatures
questions.hint: Think about what is drilled out of an ice sheet

questions.text: What term means reducing the causes of climate change, for example by cutting carbon emissions? Give the term.

feedback.adaptation: Adaptation means adjusting to the effects of climate change, such as building flood defences

questions.solution: Mitigation means tackling the causes of climate change, for example with renewable energy
questions.hint: It is the opposite strategy to adjusting to the effects

questions.text: What name is given to the zone around the Pacific Ocean where many earthquakes and volcanoes occur? Give the name.
questions.solution: The Ring of Fire follows the plate boundaries around the edge of the Pacific Ocean
questions.hint: It forms a horseshoe shape around the Pacific

questions.text: Earthquake 1 had a magnitude of 6.0 and caused many more deaths than Earthquake 2, which had a magnitude of 8.0. Which factor could explain this?

options: Earthquake 1 happened at a constructive boundary
Earthquake 1 happened far out at sea
Earthquake 1 hit a poorer area with weaker buildings and fewer emergency services

questions.solution: Deaths depend on wealth, building quality, preparation and population as well as magnitude
questions.hint: Magnitude is not the only thing that decides the number of deaths

questions.text: A hurricane's central air pressure falls from 990 mb to 940 mb over two days. What does this suggest?

options: The storm has moved over land
The storm has turned into a typhoon
feedback: Storms usually weaken over land, and their pressure rises

questions.solution: Lower central pressure means stronger winds, so the storm is intensifying
questions.hint: Think about the link between low pressure and wind speed

questions.text: Which of these is an example of PLANNING to reduce the impact of a volcanic eruption?

options: Measuring gas coming out of the crater
Creating exclusion zones and evacuation routes
Using tiltmeters to detect the ground swelling
feedback: That is monitoring, not planning
That is monitoring, not planning
That is monitoring, not planning

questions.solution: Exclusion zones and evacuation routes are planning; the other options are monitoring
questions.hint: Monitoring measures the volcano; planning prepares the people

questions.text: Which statement about global atmospheric circulation is accurate?

options: Air sinks at the equator, creating deserts
There is no wind between the tropics
Air rises at the equator, creating low pressure and heavy rainfall
High pressure at the equator causes tropical storms
feedback: Air sinks at about 30° north and south, creating high pressure and deserts

questions.solution: Warm air rises at the equator, cools and condenses, giving low pressure and heavy rain
questions.hint: Think about why rainforests are found near the equator

questions.text: A tropical storm pushes sea water onto the land and floods the coast. What is this rise in sea level called? Give the term.
questions.solution: A storm surge is caused by strong winds pushing water ashore and very low air pressure
questions.hint: It is caused by strong winds and very low air pressure

questions.text: Describe two ways people can reduce the effects of earthquakes.

rubric.model_answer: Buildings can be designed to withstand shaking, for example with rubber shock absorbers in the foundations, cross-bracing in the walls and counterweights on the roof. People can also be prepared through planning: earthquake drills in schools, emergency kits and evacuation plans. Monitoring and warning systems can give a few seconds of warning so trains stop and people take cover.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one method (e.g. earthquake-resistant buildings)
1 mark: supporting detail
1 mark: identifies a second method (e.g. planning, drills, warnings)
1 mark: supporting detail

questions.solution: Strong building design and good planning both reduce the effects of earthquakes
questions.hint: Think about buildings and about people

questions.text: Which of these is a reason people continue to live near active volcanoes?

options: Volcanoes never erupt without months of warning
Lava flows are easy to stop
Volcanic soils are very fertile for farming

questions.solution: Fertile soils, geothermal energy, tourism and minerals attract people to volcanic areas
questions.hint: Think about what volcanic ash does to soil

questions.text: Which statement explains why destructive plate boundaries have explosive volcanoes?

options: The sinking plate melts, forming thick, gas-rich magma that rises
The plates move apart, letting runny lava escape gently
The plates slide past each other without melting
There is no magma at destructive boundaries
feedback: That describes a constructive boundary

questions.solution: When the oceanic plate subducts and melts, thick, sticky magma traps gas, causing explosive eruptions
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the oceanic plate at a destructive boundary

questions.text: Which statement about the evidence for climate change is accurate?

options: There is no evidence that sea levels have changed
Ice cores, tree rings and temperature records all show the climate has changed
The climate has never changed naturally
Only one type of evidence exists

questions.solution: Many independent types of evidence show that the climate has changed over time
questions.hint: Think about the different types of evidence scientists use

questions.text: Why are lower-income countries often worse affected by tropical storms than higher-income countries?

options: Storms are always stronger in lower-income countries
Higher-income countries never have tropical storms
They may have fewer resources for warnings, strong buildings and emergency response
Lower-income countries are all far from the coast

questions.solution: Less money for prediction, warning systems, strong buildings and rescue means more people are affected
questions.hint: Think about what money can pay for before and after a storm

questions.text: Which statement about how climate change may affect tropical storms is accurate?

options: Climate change will stop all tropical storms
Tropical storms will form only at the poles
Warmer oceans may make the strongest storms more intense

questions.solution: Scientists expect warmer seas to make the most intense storms stronger and wetter
questions.hint: Remember what tropical storms need in order to form

questions.text: Explain how a tropical storm forms.

rubric.model_answer: Tropical storms form over warm oceans of about 27°C, roughly between 5° and 30° north and south of the equator. Warm, moist air rises quickly, creating an area of very low pressure. As the air rises it cools and condenses, releasing heat that powers the storm and forming huge clouds. The Coriolis effect makes the storm spin, and more air is drawn in at the surface. Cool air sinks in the centre to form the calm eye.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: warm ocean (about 27°C) between about 5° and 30° from the equator
1 mark: warm, moist air rises, giving low pressure
1 mark: condensation releases heat that powers the storm
1 mark: the Coriolis effect makes it spin / sinking air forms the eye

questions.solution: Warm seas, rising air, condensation and the Coriolis effect create tropical storms
questions.hint: Start with the conditions needed over the sea

questions.text: Which erosion process happens when rocks carried by a river or the sea grind against the bed or the cliffs?

feedback: Attrition is when rocks knock against each other and become smaller and rounder
Solution is when rock dissolves in the water
Hydraulic action is the force of the water itself

questions.solution: Abrasion is rocks scraping and grinding against the bed, banks or cliffs, wearing them away
questions.hint: Think of sandpaper rubbing a surface

questions.text: What is the process that moves sediment along a beach in a zigzag called? Give the term.
questions.solution: In longshore drift, swash carries sediment up the beach at an angle and backwash pulls it straight down
questions.hint: The swash moves material up the beach at an angle, then the backwash pulls it straight down

questions.text: What is the movement of a wave up the beach called?

feedback: Backwash is the water flowing back down the beach
Fetch is the distance of open water the wind has blown over
A spit is a landform

questions.solution: Swash is the water moving up the beach after a wave breaks
questions.hint: It is the opposite of backwash

questions.text: What is the lake called that forms when a meander is cut off from the river? Give the term.
questions.solution: An ox-bow lake forms when the river cuts through the neck of a meander and the old bend is sealed off
questions.hint: It is named after part of the wooden collar of an ox's harness

questions.text: Which landform is left when a stack collapses and is worn down?
questions.solution: Crack, cave, arch, stack, then stump
questions.hint: It is the last stage after the stack

questions.text: What is the boundary between two drainage basins called? Give the term.
questions.solution: The watershed is the edge of a drainage basin, usually along high ground
questions.hint: It usually runs along high ground

questions.text: Which statement describes a constructive wave?

options: Backwash is stronger than swash, so it erodes beaches
Constructive waves only form in rivers
A constructive wave is always taller than a destructive wave
Swash is stronger than backwash, so it builds up beaches
feedback: That describes a destructive wave

questions.solution: Constructive waves have a strong swash and weak backwash, so they deposit material
questions.hint: Constructive means building up

questions.text: What is the place where two rivers join called?

feedback: The source is where a river begins
The mouth is where a river reaches the sea
A tributary is a smaller river that joins a larger one

questions.solution: A confluence is where two rivers meet
questions.hint: Think of two flows coming together

questions.text: What does the lag time on a flood hydrograph show?

options: The total amount of rain that fell
The time between peak rainfall and peak discharge
The highest discharge of the river
feedback: The highest discharge is the peak discharge

questions.solution: Lag time is the delay between the heaviest rain and the highest river discharge
questions.hint: Lag means delay

questions.text: What are the raised banks of sediment called that build up along a river during floods? Give the term.
questions.solution: Levees form because the river drops its heaviest sediment first, close to the channel, during floods
questions.hint: They form because the river drops its heaviest sediment first, close to the channel

questions.text: What is a long, narrow ridge of sand or shingle that sticks out into the sea from the coast called? Give the term.

feedback.bar: A bar stretches right across a bay, joining two headlands
feedback.tombolo: A tombolo joins an island to the mainland

questions.solution: A spit forms where longshore drift carries sediment past a bend in the coast
questions.hint: Spurn Head in Yorkshire is a famous example

questions.text: Which hard engineering structures are built at right angles to the beach to trap sediment moved by longshore drift?

feedback: Sea walls run along the coast to reflect waves
Rock armour is boulders placed at the foot of cliffs
Beach nourishment is soft engineering: adding sand or shingle to a beach

questions.solution: Groynes are wooden or rock barriers that trap sediment and widen the beach
questions.hint: Look for the structures that stick out across the beach

questions.text: A coastline has alternating bands of hard rock and soft rock that run at right angles to the coast. Which landforms are likely to form?
questions.solution: The soft rock erodes faster into bays, leaving the hard rock sticking out as headlands
questions.hint: Think about which rock wears away faster

questions.text: On the outside bend of a meander, the water flows fastest. What happens there?

feedback: Slip-off slopes form on the inside bend, where water is slow

questions.solution: Fast, deep water on the outside bend erodes the bank into a river cliff
questions.hint: Fast water has more energy

questions.text: A town plants trees on the hills upstream to reduce flooding. What type of flood management is this?
questions.solution: Planting trees (afforestation) is soft engineering: trees intercept rain and slow the flow to the river
questions.hint: No large structures are built

questions.text: A river flows over a band of hard rock lying on top of softer rock. Which landform is likely to form?
questions.solution: The soft rock is eroded faster, undercutting the hard rock and forming a waterfall
questions.hint: Think about what happens when the softer rock below wears away

questions.text: Which type of weathering happens when water gets into cracks, freezes, expands and breaks the rock apart? Give the term.
questions.solution: In freeze-thaw weathering, water expands by about 10% when it freezes, widening cracks until rock breaks off
questions.hint: It happens when temperatures go above and below 0°C again and again

questions.text: What is it called when sand or shingle is added to a beach to make it wider and protect the coast? Give the term.
questions.solution: Beach nourishment is soft engineering that widens the beach so it absorbs wave energy
questions.hint: It is a soft engineering method

questions.text: On a flood hydrograph, peak rainfall is at 10:00 and peak discharge is at 16:00. What is the lag time?
questions.solution: Lag time = 16:00 − 10:00 = 6 hours
questions.hint: Subtract the time of peak rainfall from the time of peak discharge

questions.text: Fields in a river basin are built over with roads and houses. How is its flood hydrograph likely to change?

options: Shorter lag time and higher peak discharge
Longer lag time and lower peak discharge

questions.solution: Impermeable surfaces and drains send water to the river faster, so lag time falls and the peak rises
questions.hint: Think about what happens to rain that falls on tarmac

questions.text: A crack in a headland is eroded into a cave. Which landform forms next?
questions.solution: The cave is eroded right through the headland to form an arch, which later collapses to leave a stack
questions.hint: Think about the cave being eroded right through the headland

questions.text: The Bradshaw model shows how a river changes from source to mouth. Which statement is accurate?
questions.solution: Downstream, discharge, width, depth and velocity increase, while gradient and sediment size decrease
questions.hint: Think about how much water a river carries near its mouth

questions.text: Which waterfall on the River Tees in northern England formed where the river flows over a band of hard rock called the Whin Sill? Give the name.
questions.solution: High Force formed where the Tees flows over hard dolerite (the Whin Sill) on top of softer rock
questions.hint: Its name describes its height and power

questions.text: Describe how a waterfall forms.

rubric.model_answer: A waterfall forms where a river flows over a band of hard rock lying on top of softer rock. The softer rock is eroded faster by hydraulic action and abrasion, undercutting the hard rock and leaving an overhang. A deep plunge pool forms at the base. Eventually the overhang is unsupported and collapses into the plunge pool, and the process repeats, so the waterfall retreats upstream and leaves a steep-sided gorge.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: hard rock on top of soft rock
1 mark: soft rock eroded faster, undercutting and an overhang
1 mark: plunge pool forms
1 mark: overhang collapses and the waterfall retreats, forming a gorge

questions.solution: Undercutting of soft rock beneath hard rock makes the overhang collapse and the waterfall retreat
questions.hint: Start with the two types of rock

questions.text: Which statement about hard and soft engineering on coasts is accurate?

options: Hard engineering never affects other places
Soft engineering stops all erosion for ever
Hard engineering is often expensive and can increase erosion further along the coast

questions.solution: Hard defences cost a lot and can starve beaches further along the coast of sediment
questions.hint: Think about where the sediment trapped by defences would have gone

questions.text: Why might groynes at one town increase erosion at a village further along the coast?

options: They trap sediment, so less reaches the beaches further along to protect them
They block rivers from reaching the sea

questions.solution: With less sediment arriving, beaches further along become narrower and cliffs behind them erode faster
questions.hint: Think about the direction of longshore drift

questions.text: Why is the Holderness coast in East Yorkshire eroding so quickly?

options: The cliffs are made of very hard granite
The cliffs are made of soft boulder clay that is easily eroded
A wide beach protects the whole coast

questions.solution: Holderness has soft boulder clay cliffs and narrow beaches, so destructive waves erode it quickly
questions.hint: Think about the type of rock in the cliffs

questions.text: Why do ox-bow lakes often form during floods?

options: People dig them to store water
The river cuts through the narrow neck of a meander, and deposition seals off the old bend

questions.solution: In a flood the river takes the shortest route through the neck; deposition then cuts off the old loop
questions.hint: Think about the shortest route for flood water

questions.text: Which statement about managed retreat is accurate?

options: A new sea wall is built further out to sea
Groynes are added to the beach
Rock armour is placed at the base of the cliffs
Land is allowed to flood or erode in a controlled way, creating habitats such as salt marsh

questions.solution: Managed retreat lets the sea flood low-value land, creating salt marsh that absorbs wave energy
questions.hint: Retreat means moving back

questions.text: Explain how a spit is formed.

rubric.model_answer: Longshore drift carries sand and shingle along the coast in the direction of the prevailing wind. Where the coastline changes direction, for example at a river mouth or a bend in the coast, the material continues to be deposited out into the sea, forming a long ridge. Changes in wind direction can curve the end of the spit, forming a hooked end. The sheltered area behind the spit often becomes a salt marsh.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: longshore drift moves sediment along the coast
1 mark: the coastline changes direction
1 mark: deposition continues out into the sea, forming a ridge
1 mark: wind changes curve the end / salt marsh forms behind

questions.solution: Longshore drift keeps depositing sediment where the coast changes direction
questions.hint: Start with the process that moves sediment along the coast

questions.text: What term describes an increase in the proportion of people living in towns and cities? Give the term.

feedback.suburbanisation: Suburbanisation is people moving from the inner city to the edge of the city
feedback.counter-urbanisation: Counter-urbanisation is people moving out of cities into the countryside

questions.solution: Urbanisation is the growth in the share of people living in urban areas
questions.hint: It comes from the Latin word urbs, meaning city

questions.text: What is a megacity?

options: A city with more than 10 million people
A city with more than 1 million people
A city with more than 100,000 people

questions.solution: A megacity has a population of over 10 million
questions.hint: Mega means very large

questions.text: What does HDI stand for? Give the full name.
questions.solution: The Human Development Index combines life expectancy, education and income
questions.hint: It combines life expectancy, education and income

questions.text: Which of these is an economic measure of development?

feedback: Life expectancy is a social measure
Literacy rate is a social measure
Infant mortality is a social measure

questions.solution: GNI per head measures a country's income per person
questions.hint: Look for the measure that is about money

questions.text: What is a 'pull factor' in migration?

options: Something that makes people leave, such as drought
Something that attracts people to a new place, such as jobs
feedback: That is a push factor

questions.solution: Pull factors attract people to a place; push factors drive them away
questions.hint: Pull means drawing something towards you

questions.text: What term is used for homes built informally on land the residents do not own, often on the edge of cities in poorer countries? Give the term.
questions.solution: Squatter settlements are built informally, often without clean water, sanitation or electricity
questions.hint: Brazil and India have well-known examples

questions.text: In which stage of the Demographic Transition Model does the population grow fastest, because death rates fall but birth rates stay high?

feedback: In Stage 1 birth and death rates are both high, so growth is slow
In Stage 4 both rates are low
In Stage 5 the population may start to fall

questions.solution: In Stage 2 the death rate falls quickly but the birth rate stays high, so the population grows rapidly
questions.hint: Look for the biggest gap between birth rate and death rate

questions.text: Which describes a brownfield site?

options: Land that has been built on before and can be redeveloped
Land that has never been built on
A park in a city centre
feedback: Land that has never been built on is a greenfield site

questions.solution: Brownfield sites are old industrial or previously developed land that can be reused
questions.hint: Think about old factory land

questions.text: What is the informal economy?

options: Work that is not officially registered or taxed, such as street selling
Jobs in large factories with contracts

questions.solution: Informal jobs are unregistered and untaxed, with no contracts or protection
questions.hint: Informal means unofficial

questions.text: What term describes people moving out of large cities to live in smaller towns and the countryside? Give the term.

feedback.urbanisation: Urbanisation is the growth of towns and cities; this is the opposite movement
feedback.suburbanisation: Suburbanisation is moving to the edge of the same city

questions.solution: Counter-urbanisation is the movement of people from cities into rural areas
questions.hint: The first part of the word means against or opposite

questions.text: What is a large company that operates in more than one country called? Give the term.
questions.solution: Transnational corporations (TNCs) have offices or factories in several countries
questions.hint: Examples include large car and technology firms

questions.text: Which of these describes globalisation?

options: People moving from cities into the countryside
A country cutting all its trade links
The growing connections between countries through trade, communication and culture
The growth of a single village
feedback: That is counter-urbanisation

questions.solution: Globalisation means the world becoming more interconnected
questions.hint: Global means worldwide

questions.text: A city's population grows from 2 million to 12 million. What can the city now be called?
questions.solution: With over 10 million people it is a megacity
questions.hint: Compare 12 million with 10 million

questions.text: A cocoa farmer in Ghana receives a guaranteed minimum price plus an extra payment to invest in the community. Which scheme is this?

feedback: Debt relief cancels money a country owes
Microfinance gives small loans
Tied aid must be spent on goods from the donor country

questions.solution: Fairtrade guarantees farmers a minimum price and a premium for community projects
questions.hint: Think about a fair price for producers

questions.text: A woman in a low-income country gets a small loan to start a sewing business. What is this called?
questions.solution: Microfinance gives small loans to people who cannot borrow from ordinary banks
questions.hint: Micro means very small

questions.text: A country has a birth rate of 40 per 1,000 and a death rate of 35 per 1,000. Which stage of the Demographic Transition Model fits best?

feedback: In Stage 3 the birth rate is falling and the death rate is already low
In Stage 4 both rates are low

questions.solution: Both rates are high and close together, which fits Stage 1
questions.hint: Are both rates high or low?

questions.text: Which former port area of East London was redeveloped from the 1980s, with offices at Canary Wharf? Give the name.
questions.solution: The London Docklands were regenerated after the docks closed, with offices, homes and new transport
questions.hint: Ships used to unload cargo here

questions.text: What term describes a city's built-up area spreading out into the surrounding countryside? Give the term.

feedback.urbanisation: Urbanisation is the growing share of people living in towns and cities; the spreading out has another name

questions.solution: Urban sprawl is the outward spread of a city, often onto greenfield land
questions.hint: It often eats into green belt land

questions.text: Country P has a GNI per head of 50,000 US dollars and an HDI of 0.93. Country Q has a GNI per head of 1,000 US dollars and an HDI of 0.45. Which statement is accurate?

options: Country Q is more developed on both measures
The two countries are equally developed
Country P is more developed than Country Q on both measures

questions.solution: Country P has a higher income and a higher HDI, so it is more developed on both measures
questions.hint: A higher HDI, closer to 1, means more developed

questions.text: A country has 8 million people aged 0–14, 10 million aged 15–64 and 2 million aged 65 or over. What is its dependency ratio?

feedback: Include the over-65s as well as the children

questions.hint: Add the young and old dependants, then divide by the working-age population and multiply by 100

questions.text: Which of these is a PUSH factor that makes people leave rural areas in a low-income country?

options: More schools and hospitals in the city
Entertainment and bright lights in the city
feedback: That is a pull factor
That is a pull factor
That is a pull factor

questions.solution: Crop failure pushes people away from rural areas; the others pull people towards cities
questions.hint: A push factor is about the place people are leaving

questions.text: A city adds bus lanes, cycle paths and a tram system. Which sustainable urban aim does this support?
questions.solution: Better public transport and cycling cut congestion and air pollution
questions.hint: Think about what happens to car journeys

questions.text: Which Rio de Janeiro project improved favelas by adding paved roads, water supply and sewers instead of demolishing them? Give its name.
questions.solution: The Favela Bairro Project upgraded favelas with services, roads and community facilities
questions.hint: Its name means 'favela to neighbourhood' in Portuguese

questions.text: Describe two ways the development gap could be reduced.

rubric.model_answer: International aid can pay for projects such as schools, clean water and health care; small-scale intermediate technology, such as hand water pumps, can be run by local communities. Fair trade gives farmers a fair price and a premium for community projects, raising incomes. Debt relief lets governments spend on services instead of interest, and microfinance loans help people start small businesses.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one strategy (e.g. aid)
1 mark: explains how it reduces the gap
1 mark: identifies a second strategy (e.g. fair trade, debt relief, microfinance)
1 mark: explains how it reduces the gap

questions.solution: Aid, fair trade, debt relief and microfinance can all reduce the development gap
questions.hint: Think about money, trade and debt

questions.text: Which statement about urbanisation is accurate?

options: Cities in high-income countries are growing fastest
Fewer than 10% of the world's people live in cities
In recent decades most urban growth has been in lower-income and emerging countries

questions.solution: Cities in lower-income and emerging countries are growing fastest, through migration and natural increase
questions.hint: Think about where megacities have grown fastest

questions.text: Why does the death rate fall in Stage 2 of the Demographic Transition Model?

options: Improvements in health care, clean water and food supply
People choose to have fewer children
feedback: Fewer children affects the birth rate, which falls in Stage 3

questions.solution: Better medicine, clean water, sanitation and food supply mean fewer people die young
questions.hint: Think about what keeps people alive for longer

questions.text: Which statement about the Human Development Index is accurate?

options: HDI combines health, education and income into a value from 0 to 1
A higher value means a country is less developed
HDI is measured in US dollars

questions.solution: HDI uses life expectancy, education and income to give a value between 0 and 1
questions.hint: Think about the three things the HDI measures

questions.text: Which is a disadvantage of building new homes on greenfield sites?

options: Old pollution has to be cleaned up first
It destroys countryside and wildlife habitats
feedback: Cleaning up old pollution is a problem of brownfield sites

questions.solution: Building on greenfield land uses up countryside and habitats and increases urban sprawl
questions.hint: Greenfield land has never been built on

questions.text: Which statement about transnational corporations (TNCs) in lower-income countries is accurate?

options: They always pay higher taxes than local firms
They are owned by the local government
They can create jobs, but profits may go back to the country where the TNC is based

questions.solution: TNCs bring jobs and investment, but profits often leave the country and working conditions can be poor
questions.hint: Think about both the benefits and the problems

questions.text: Explain two challenges caused by rapid urban growth in cities in lower-income or emerging countries.

rubric.model_answer: Rapid growth means housing cannot be built fast enough, so many people live in squatter settlements without clean water, sanitation or electricity, which helps disease spread. Many new arrivals cannot find formal jobs and work in the informal economy with low, insecure pay and no protection. Traffic congestion and air pollution also increase, and waste collection struggles to keep up.
rubric.mark_scheme:
1 mark: identifies one challenge (e.g. housing and services)
1 mark: explains its effect
1 mark: identifies a second challenge (e.g. informal jobs, congestion, pollution)
1 mark: explains its effect

questions.solution: Housing, services, jobs and pollution are all challenges of rapid urban growth
questions.hint: Think about homes, jobs and the environment
